title: Psammetichus I
summary: King of Egypt (Saite line); Herodotus says Greek knowledge of Egyptian history is accurate from his reign onward (2.151–157).
description: Added from the Herodotus import (The Histories, tr. Rawlinson). Herodotus gives reign lengths and synchronisms, not BC years, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Herodotus is display-only and gives none).

reign.date: “before the reign of their king Psammetichus, believed themselves to be the most ancient of mankind”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.2 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 96 (PDF p. 98)
reign.note: Psammetichus's experiment on the oldest language; afterwards the Egyptians granted the Phrygians greater antiquity.

reign.date: “he had fled from Sabacos the Ethiopian, who had put his father Necos to death”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.152 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 162 (PDF p. 164)
reign.note: Synchronism: Psammetichus's first exile was under Sabacos.

reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.154 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 164 (PDF p. 166)
reign.note: Herodotus: through the Greek settlers, the Greeks know Egyptian history accurately from Psammetichus onward.

reign.date: “Psammetichus ruled Egypt for fifty-four years, during twenty-nine of which he pressed the siege of Azotus without intermission”
reign.citation: Herodotus, Histories 2.157 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 165 (PDF p. 167)
reign.note: Azotus = Ashdod. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): Saite reigns back from the conquest by Cambyses (CFAH AP-8, 525 BC): Psammenitus ½ + Amasis 44 + Apries 25 + Psammis 6 + Necos 16 + Psammetichus 54 = 145½ years, so Psammetichus came to the throne about 671/670 BC (approximate).
